title: Twisted boundary-ideal quotient and its residue-one section
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $x\in X$ a point with closed singleton, $U\subseteq X$ an affine open containing $x$, and $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] with free generator $e$ on $U$. Put $Z=X\setminus U$ and $Z'=Z\cup\{x\}$. For either closed subset $T$, let $\mathcal I_T(V)=\{b\in\mathcal O_X(V):b(t)=0\text{ in }\kappa(t)\text{ for all }t\in T\cap V\}$ be its reduced vanishing ideal [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme, def-weil-residue-field]. Write $\mathcal I=\mathcal I_Z$, $\mathcal J=\mathcal I_{Z'}$, and $\mathcal Q=\mathcal I/\mathcal J$, the sheafification of the sectionwise quotient in the category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then $\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal J$ are quasi-coherent ideal sheaves [pqf-def-coherent], $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal I$, $\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U$, $\mathcal I|_{X\setminus\{x\}}=\mathcal J|_{X\setminus\{x\}}$, and $\mathcal J_x=\mathfrak m_x\subseteq\mathcal I_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. For every integer $n\ge1$, put $\mathcal M_n=\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The canonical sequence
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal J\otimes\mathcal M_n\longrightarrow\mathcal I\otimes\mathcal M_n\xrightarrow{\pi_n}\mathcal Q\otimes\mathcal M_n\longrightarrow0$$
is short exact, and the canonical map $\iota_n:\mathcal I\otimes\mathcal M_n\to\mathcal M_n$ is injective. There exists a global section $q_n\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal Q\otimes\mathcal M_n)$ whose restriction to $U$ is $\pi_n(e^{\otimes n})$, using $\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U$, and whose restriction to $X\setminus\{x\}$ is zero. The canonical quotient identification $(\mathcal Q\otimes\mathcal M_n)_x\cong(\mathcal M_n)_x/\mathfrak m_x(\mathcal M_n)_x$, induced by $\iota_n$, takes $(q_n)_x$ to the class of $e_x^{\otimes n}$; in its generator coordinate this is $1\in\kappa(x)$, in particular nonzero.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme](1) to the closed subsets $Z$ and $Z^{\prime}$: both ideals are quasi-coherent, with exactly the residue-vanishing description in the statement. Since $Z\subseteq Z^{\prime}$, vanishing on $Z^{\prime}$ implies vanishing on $Z$, so $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal I$. On every open $W\subseteq U$, $Z\cap W=\varnothing$, and hence $\mathcal I(W)=\mathcal O_X(W)$. Put $V=X\setminus\{x\}$, which is open by the closed-point hypothesis. On every open $W\subseteq V$, $Z^{\prime}\cap W=Z\cap W$, so $\mathcal I(W)=\mathcal J(W)$. These equalities commute with restrictions and give the asserted equalities of restricted sheaves.

Use the germ description [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] and $\kappa(x)=\mathcal O_{X,x}/\mathfrak m_x$ [def-weil-residue-field]. We already have $\mathcal I_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$. If a germ comes from $\mathcal J$, its residue is zero, so it belongs to $\mathfrak m_x$. Conversely, represent any $a\in\mathfrak m_x$ by a section $b$ on a neighbourhood $W\subseteq U$ of $x$. Its residue at $x$ is zero. Since $Z^{\prime}\cap W=\{x\}$, this is precisely the condition $b\in\mathcal J(W)$. Thus $\mathcal J_x=\mathfrak m_x$. The quotient $\mathcal Q$ is the cokernel of the ideal inclusion in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact](1),(3),(5), its canonical sequence is short exact, $\mathcal Q_x\cong\mathcal O_{X,x}/\mathfrak m_x$, and $\mathcal Q_y=0$ for $y\in V$, because $\mathcal J_y=\mathcal I_y$. A section all of whose germs are zero vanishes on a neighbourhood of each point and hence is zero by sheaf locality; consequently $\mathcal Q|_V=0$.

Here is the local tensor calculation, directly from [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. On any open $W$ with a free generator $f$ of $\mathcal L|_W$, induction on $n$ gives the generator $f^{\otimes n}$ of $\mathcal M_n|_W$. For every module sheaf $\mathcal F$, the coefficient map on local pure tensors is $a\otimes(b f^{\otimes n})\mapsto ba$, with inverse $a\mapsto a\otimes f^{\otimes n}$. The balancing relation proves that the first map is well-defined, and both composites are the identity on pure tensors, hence on finite sums. These maps commute with restriction. They therefore extend over sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]: by [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-sheafification-space] every germ of a section of the sheafified tensor product is the image of a germ of a local presheaf tensor, and two local presheaf tensors with the same image have the same germ; so local tensor representatives are sent to the displayed coefficients, which agree on overlaps and glue in $\mathcal F$; the two inverse identities remain true locally and hence globally on $W$. Thus $(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal M_n)|_W\cong\mathcal F|_W$, naturally in $\mathcal F$. Such $W$ cover $X$ by [def-sc-invertible-module].

proof.text: Apply the coordinate isomorphisms of Step 3 to $\mathcal F=\mathcal J,\mathcal I,\mathcal Q,\mathcal O_X$ on each trivializing $W$. Naturality identifies the two maps of the twisted sequence with $\mathcal J|_W\to\mathcal I|_W\to\mathcal Q|_W$, and identifies $\iota_n$ with $\mathcal I|_W\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_W$. For each $y\in W$, these identifications give the short exact stalk sequence of Step 2 and an injective inclusion. Since the $W$ cover $X$, [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact](5) proves exactness everywhere, while (1),(3),(5) applied with zero end terms give the stated monomorphism and epimorphism assertions. This proves short exactness and injectivity of $\iota_n$ without assuming that taking sections preserves epimorphisms. The same coordinates with $\mathcal F=\mathcal Q$ show $(\mathcal Q\otimes\mathcal M_n)|_V=0$.

Fix $n\geq1$. On $U$, the generator $e^{\otimes n}$ defines a section of $\mathcal I\otimes\mathcal M_n$ because $\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U$; let $a_U$ be its image under $\pi_n$. On $V$ choose the zero section. Their restrictions to $U\cap V$ agree, since the quotient twist is zero there by Step 4. The opens $U,V$ cover $X$: a point outside $V$ equals $x$ and lies in $U$. The sheaf gluing axiom, part of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], now gives $q_n$ with exactly the two required restrictions. This uses no lift on global sections.

At $x$, the $e^{\otimes n}$ coordinate of Step 3 identifies $(\mathcal I\otimes\mathcal M_n)_x$ with $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $(\mathcal J\otimes\mathcal M_n)_x$ with $\mathfrak m_x$, by Step 2. In the target $(\mathcal M_n)_x$, $\iota_n$ sends $a\otimes b e_x^{\otimes n}$ to $ab e_x^{\otimes n}$. Thus its image is all of $(\mathcal M_n)_x$, and the image of the twisted $\mathcal J$ is exactly $\mathfrak m_x(\mathcal M_n)_x$. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] applied to the twisted quotient map gives the asserted canonical quotient identification, induced by this very map $\iota_n$. By restriction to $U$ and the germ rule [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], $(q_n)_x$ is the image of $e_x^{\otimes n}$. Its coefficient modulo $\mathfrak m_x$ is $1$ in the field $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field], so is nonzero.
